summary: Llama-3 architecture support (optional rope_freqs.weight per-pair frequency factors = the baked llama3 RoPE scaling, plus key_length/value_length/vocab_size architecture-aware validation) and a larger Qwen2.5-1.5B model, both validated end-to-end on the custom out-of-core streamed CPU decoder against the resident llama.cpp reference. No custom quant kernels; dequant/matvec remain pinned ggml traits.

git.note: Evidence produced against the committed llama-3 implementation source in this session's local commits.

environment.host: Windows 11 + WSL2 Ubuntu, Intel i5-12400F (12 logical CPUs), CPU-only

llama3_architecture_audit.identifier_hazard: Llama-3 GGUFs use general.architecture == 'llama' (same id as Stories/Llama-2). The decoder must NOT assume the Stories math from the id alone.

found_in_pinned_reference_and_real_gguf.rope_scaling: the HF 'llama3' rope scaling is baked at conversion time into a global rope_freqs.weight tensor (head_dim/2 F32 factors). Runtime applies it as ggml freq_factors: theta_pair_j = (pos * theta_scale^j) / rope_freqs[j].
found_in_pinned_reference_and_real_gguf.extra_metadata: llama.attention.key_length, llama.attention.value_length, llama.vocab_size (not present on Stories models)
found_in_pinned_reference_and_real_gguf.gqa: 32 query heads / 8 kv heads (4:1) - already supported

llama3_architecture_audit.implemented: Accept optional rope_freqs.weight (head_dim/2 F32); read once per token; divide each RoPE pair angle by its factor (applies to both normal and NeoX branches). Allow key_length/value_length/vocab_size keys and validate them (key_length==value_length==head_dim, vocab_size==tokenizer count) else reject. Tensor-count guard admits exactly one optional global extra tensor (rope_freqs.weight).
llama3_architecture_audit.rejection_before_change: Prior to this change the decoder safely REJECTED Llama-3 GGUFs (unknown llama.vocab_size key failed the allowlist; rope_freqs.weight failed the tensor-count guard) - no silent wrong inference.

Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.coverage: 113/113 eligible weight tensors are K-quant (all rows 256-divisible); 34 F32 = 32 norms + output_norm + rope_freqs.weight[32]

Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.coverage: 197/197 eligible weight tensors are K-quant (dim 1536 and n_ff 8960 both 256-divisible); 141 F32 = 56 norms + 84 Q/K/V biases + output_norm

bounded_memory.method: streamed backend, --address-space-mb enforces Linux RLIMIT_AS; ctx 64, threads 2, max_tokens 8, workspace 24 MB.
bounded_memory.finding: Both run under a 256 MB address-space limit at ~62-76 MB peak RSS. RSS is dominated by the large vocab-only tokenizer (128256 / 151936 tokens), NOT the ~0.8-1.0 GB model weights. Out-of-core weight streaming holds: RSS is decoupled from model file size.
bounded_memory.note: RLIMIT_AS is a process address-space bound, not physical RAM; passing under 256 MB RLIMIT_AS on WSL2 does not by itself prove physical 2 GB device compatibility.

cpu_affinity.method: taskset pins the process to specific logical CPUs (verified via /proc/self/status Cpus_allowed_list), separate from the --threads count.
cpu_affinity.model: Llama-3.2-1B-Q4_K_M, prompt 'Once upon a time', ctx 128, max_tokens 16
cpu_affinity.finding: Real 2-core OS affinity verified. Going 2->4 cores/threads improves wall time only marginally (7.50s -> 6.84s, not ~2x) because streamed inference is I/O-bound on per-token weight re-streaming, not compute-bound. --threads alone does not constrain cores; taskset does.

storage_io.method: streamed --metrics, ctx 64, threads 2, max_tokens 8, cache disabled.
storage_io.analysis: Each forward pass re-streams the full weight set (no persistent weight residency), so source bytes ~= (prefill + generated tokens) x model payload, giving ~10x amplification for an 8-token workload. This is the documented synchronous per-token re-stream design; the consumption-time re-read is a mutation-detection security dependency and is not removed.
storage_io.remote_feasibility_derived: At ~10x amplification a remote source would need roughly model_size x tokens of transfer per request absent coalescing. For a ~0.8-1.0 GB model generating tens of tokens this implies multi-GB transfers: impractical over 10/100 Mbps, bandwidth-bound over 1 Gbps, and latency-sensitive given ~846k small range ops per the 0.5B measurement. A verified bounded cache or sealed-manifest staged-range mechanism (not implemented here) would be required; remote range-read remains future work.

backward_compatibility.stories110M_Q6_K_llama: streamed == resident EXACT (16 tokens) - the unified RoPE refactor preserves the normal-RoPE path byte-for-byte
backward_compatibility.qwen2_5_0_5b_Q8_0_qwen2: teacher-forced 15/16 unchanged from pre-llama3 change (rope refactor numerically neutral for qwen2)
backward_compatibility.conclusion: No regression from the llama-3 changes; rope_freqs path is inert when the tensor is absent.

security_regression.changes_touch: streamed decoder RoPE/metadata validation + an opt-in CLI logit dump only
security_regression.unchanged: SHA-256 authenticated source access, sealed-manifest integrity, source mutation detection, deadline/cancellation, worker lifecycle, memory admission, isfinite guards, bounded range reads; ABI version unchanged.

compatibility_matrix.Qwen2.5-1.5B Q4_K_M (qwen2, head_dim 128: VERIFIED (real inference, 197/197 K-quant, teacher-forced 12/16 all near-ties, bounded <=256 MB)
compatibility_matrix.Llama-3.2-1B Q4_K_M (llama-3 rope scalin: VERIFIED (streamed==resident EXACT, teacher-forced 16/16, 113/113 K-quant, bounded <=256 MB)

limitations: Only one Llama-3 configuration (3.2-1B) tested; other sizes and non-tied-output Llama-3 variants untested.
Llama-3 models that carry runtime llama.rope.scaling.* metadata (rather than a baked rope_freqs.weight) are rejected, not executed.

Synthetic unsupported-architecture GGUF negative integration tests not added; rejection is enforced by resolve_arch, the metadata allowlist, key_length/value_length/vocab_size validation, and the tensor-count guard (code-level), and was confirmed by Llama-3 having been rejected before this change.
cgroup memory.max and CPU quota enforcement not applied (no passwordless privilege); Windows MSVC native lane not run.
Bounded-memory tested at 256/512 MB; larger 1024/2048 MB limits have ample headroom but were not individually swept.
